newsitem.title: UK: Zaire relief effort in Bukavu "paralysed" - priest.
newsitem.headline: Zaire relief effort in Bukavu "paralysed" - priest.

text.p: A Roman Catholic priest in Bukavu in eastern Zaire said on Wednesday the town was completely cut off from aid supplies and thousands of refugees were in danger of starving to death.

"There is too little happening in the town. We are beginning to run short of food. At this rate, we are all going to die of hunger," Abbe Pierre Cibambo said in a statement issued by the charity CAFOD.
Cibambo stayed in Bukavu when many expatriate aid workers left last week following an escalation in the clashes between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsis.
He said law and order had broken down, preventing aid organisations from doing their work.
"We are totally paralysed." said Cibambo. "Humanitarian flights are impossible because of the lack of security. If we can't establish conditions for organising aid here soon, it could be too late."
He said there were 150,000 refugees in camps around Bukavu who had no access to aid.

CAFOD, the overseas development charity of the Catholic Church in England and Wales, said it had two planeloads of aid waiting to be flown into the town of Goma as soon as security could be guaranteed.
But Cibamba told the agency he saw little hope for an immediate improvement in the situation.

The Rwandan refugees in Zaire are Hutus blamed for the 1994 genocide of Tutsis. They are resisting appeals from the United Nations, regularly broadcast to them over loudspeakers, to return to Rwanda saying they fear for their lives if they return.
